source.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Implicit Bias: Generalization vs. Robustness in ReLU Networks
source.authors: Spencer Frei; Gal Vardi; P. Bartlett; N. Srebro

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Proves a related generalization result using KKT analysis in a clustered Gaussian setting, rather than testing the claim versions’ specified empirical settings or interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper proves generalization and robustness guarantees for two-layer ReLU networks on clustered data. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, the listed optimizer or regularization comparisons, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study proves generalization guarantees for clustered Gaussian data, but tests none of V1–V8. A width-independent upper bound does not establish V2's decreasing test error with increasing width, and good generalization alone does not establish V1's coexistence with random-label memorization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct but needs explicit conditions: under the clustered-data and sample-size assumptions, gradient flow that reaches empirical loss below 1/n converges in direction to a network that generalizes well, irrespective of width. When c²k grows without bound, where each label occupies at least a fraction c of clusters, these limiting networks lack sqrt(d)-scale robustness even though classifiers with that robustness exist.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical analysis of KKT points and gradient-flow convergence on a clustered Gaussian-mixture distribution; no random-label memorization experiment or listed benchmark recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantees depend on the clustered-data assumptions, sample-size conditions, loss (logistic or exponential for the gradient-flow implication), and the fraction of positive and negative clusters for the robustness result.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Assumption 2.2 and explicit sample-size and dimension conditions, every KKT point of the two-layer ReLU parameter-space maximum-margin problem has test error at most epsilon with probability at least 1−delta. Gradient flow reaching sufficiently small logistic or exponential loss converges in direction to such a point.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On the specified clustered distributions, the implicit bias of gradient flow yields a conditional, width-independent generalization guarantee, including for highly overparameterized two-layer ReLU networks.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and restricted to the paper’s clustered Gaussian-mixture assumptions and explicit sample-size conditions; it does not establish the mapped empirical claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported empirical or theoretical result matching a listed version was found. Robustness theorems were not extracted as rows because robustness is not among the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Whether increasing width beyond interpolation lowers test error; the uniform bound supplies no ordering across widths.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and initialization or learned-sparsity qualifications.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning budgets, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects, training-set size, underfitting, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures. Input adversarial robustness is a different construct.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. The study's assumptions delimit its separate theoretical result; they are not evidence limiting any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of held-out performance on natural versus random labels; no listed benchmark architectures.
No width sweep or comparison of test error across widths.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison or epoch-budget intervention.
No measurement of magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison with other generalization measures.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.
